scope: Theorem 5.4 (Concentration, injection, and Weil spanning) of the manuscript “Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration” (preprints/Rationality-of-the-Canonical-Unramified-Arthur-Filtration-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eaf8e38720714e23), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On a fixed retained spectral component, the trace of every closed invariant nilpotent support category is concentrated in degree zero. If Ω′ ⊂ Ω are such support bounds, then H0 Tr(Φ, Ind BΩ′,0) −→ H0 Tr(Φ, Ind BΩ,0) (5.8) is injective. A finite filtration by invariant unions of orbits has the orbit traces as its actual successive quotients. Every trace class is a finite linear combination of classes of compact objects with Weil structures; those objects can be chosen with support in the prescribed bound. All assertions hold on the compact opposite side. After assembling retained components, these statements apply to CY and C. In particular, the image defining FY AQℓ is the injective image of the supported trace, and every function in AQℓ and every vector in FY AQℓ is a finite linear combination of the corresponding actual compact Weil trace functions. The analogous statement supplies all tests through the nonstandard self-duality of Theorem 2.4.
